## Intent
Hypothesis: Halide-expressible math in loop1 can be auto-vectorized to approach the streaming ceiling, while the RNG-order-dependent loop2 runs as a simple serial pass.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, ns/p is flat across N: 15.555 (N=10000) → 14.683 (N=10000000), with no knee at the L2 spill (N≈61680) between them. The L1d spill (N≈963) sits below the smallest measured N. Cost slightly decreases with N — overhead amortization, not cache pressure. Death rate raises the floor without changing the shape: at q=0.5, ns/p holds ~20.3–20.5 across all N. No spill knee confirms the workload is not cache-sensitive.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 4.63 GB/s at N=10000000, q=0.01 — 15.5% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling. The algo is compute-bound: at 1 thread, q=0.01, compute is 73.5–77.2% of cycles across all N. Death rate drives the transition: branch_flush rises from 1.7% (q=0.01) to 25.8% (q=0.5) at N=10000000, eroding compute to 63.7% and raising ns/p from 14.683 to 20.48. The algo stays compute-bound throughout; branch cost scales with churn.

## Assembly
No vectorization — 0 vector-suffixed instructions. All FP is scalar: `fmul` (×4), `fadd` (×1), `fsub` (×1) on `s` registers. Particle data loads via `ldp s5, s6` and `ldr s17`. The math loop is dispatched to `_halide_b5_math` via `bl`, but the step body is scalar. The pixel scatter uses byte-granular `ldrb`/`strb` pairs (12 and 16) with `csel`-based clamping to 0xFF — read-modify-write on individual RGB bytes. No gather instruction. Scalar codegen and `strb` scatter explain the 15.5% ceiling fraction: too few memory ops per cycle to saturate the bus.

## Verdict
Refuted — the Halide-expressible math was not vectorized (0 vector-suffixed instructions), and bandwidth never exceeds 4.63 GB/s = 15.5% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling. The algo is compute-bound (76.5% compute, 1 thread, N=10000000, q=0.01), and branch_flush reaches 25.8% at q=0.5, degrading ns/p to 20.48. Scalar codegen with byte-granular `strb` scatter prevents any approach to the streaming ceiling.
